The input load `in_ptr0 + (y0 + 96*x2 + 290400*y1)` has stride-96 in the x (spatial) dimension, so consecutive threads in the x-warp lane access addresses 96 floats apart, causing non-coalesced cache line waste. The L2 is saturated at 95.6% while compute sits at 28.6%, confirming memory is the sole bottleneck. Adding tl.max_contiguous and tl.multiple_of hints on the xindex array tells the Triton compiler that accesses are contiguous and XBLOCK-aligned, enabling 128-bit (float4) vectorized loads/stores on the output dimension instead of scalar 32-bit accesses. This reduces memory transactions and relieves L2 pressure. Adding @triton.autotune explores tile configurations to find the optimal XBLOCK/YBLOCK/num_warps combination.
